messages:
maya: FYI customer 'Acme Payments' seeing intermittent 403s after they updated billing. They say there is no trace id visible in their dashboard. Quote from them: 'request failed - 403 - no request id'. Can someone advise what exact bits to ask for?

sam: Ask them for (1) the raw request/response headers (HAR or curl), (2) any SDK logs showing the request id, and (3) a short reproducible curl we can run. Also ask for the approximate client timestamp.

maya: can you paste a minimal curl snippet I can send? they aren't very technical.

sam: Sure — send this and tell them to replace the api key and prompt: 

```bash
curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_KEY>" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"gpt-4o-mini","input":"hello","max_tokens":5}'
```

sam: Important: ask them to include the full verbose output (`-v`) and paste the response headers. We're looking for any header named `x-request-id`, `x-rw-request-id`, `x-redwood-request-id` or similar.

maya: non-dev customer — how do they export a HAR? brief steps?

sam: Quick HAR guide for them: Chrome -> DevTools (F12) -> Network tab -> reproduce the request -> right-click the request -> "Save as HAR with content". Tell them to redact Authorization header before upload.

maya: mobile app — they said it's coming from Android.

sam: For Android/iOS SDKs: ask them to grep Logcat/Console for `requestId` or `Request-Id` fields. In our SDKs we log something like `Request completed id=<id> status=403` near the network line. If they can't find it, ask for the exact device timestamp + approximate user id.

lee: If they cannot capture a request id at all, we can still correlate by timestamp + client IP + user id or session id. Provide us: 
- exact ISO timestamp range (±30s)
- client IP (if available)
- account/org id + example user id
- request path (e.g. `/v1/generate`)

lee: Also remind them to include the X-Forwarded-For headers if they're behind a proxy — sometimes the edge strips original IP and we need the proxy header to match.

maya: They asked about the "debug bundle" flow — how do I generate one from Console?

sam: From Support Console -> open the customer org -> Tools -> Create debug bundle. You'll get a short token (debug_token=abc123). Tell the customer to paste the token here or attach the bundle to the ticket. We can then pull server-side traces for that window.

maya: Any privacy concerns to flag to them?

sam: Yes — ask them to redact any PII in the HAR before uploading. If they need to share an unredacted bundle, escalate to secure upload link via our support portal.

maya: I'll send a short message to the customer with the curl + HAR steps + where to find SDK logs.

dispatch-bot: Ticket #INC-2026-452 created and linked to this thread.

sam: One more tip for the message to customer — give them a tiny checklist to copy-paste: 
- Reproduce the error and save a HAR (Chrome/Edge) OR run the curl above with `-v`
- Check mobile logs for `requestId` and paste the line(s) if present
- If possible, grab a screenshot of the response headers from DevTools (Headers tab)
- If unable to capture ids, provide exact timestamps + user/session id + client IP

maya: Perfect. I'll post that now and follow up when they reply.

sam: Thanks — if they send a token or request id, ping @lee and we will pull the edge trace and correlate in the logs.

lee: If we see an auth-related 403, first check the auth service logs for token introspection traces; often it's an expired billing plan flag. If there's a mismatch we can usually point to the entitlement check id in the trace.

maya: done, customer sent back a HAR and a screenshot with response headers — I attached them to the ticket and redacted auth.

sam: Great, forwarding to @lee. Thanks!
